summary: Moody's downgraded the U.S. credit rating on May 16, making it the first time all three major agencies have stripped the U.S. of their top rating. The immediate reaction saw stocks sell off and the 30-year Treasury yield jump above 5%, hammering long-duration bonds and keeping real rates elevated. Separately, fraying U.S.-Iran ceasefire talks keep an oil risk premium embedded in markets, with WTI near $105.
tweet: Moody's stripped the U.S. of its last triple-A rating as Iran tensions hold oil near $105 — long bonds are taking the hit across the board.
